name: Nicodemus
charge: Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?; and bringing a hundred pound weight of myrrh and aloes
summary: A Pharisee and ruler of the Jews came to Christ by night, acknowledged that his works showed God was with him, and was told that a man must be born again to see the kingdom of God (John 3:1-3). He was asked whether he was a master of Israel and did not know these things (John 3:9-10). When the council raged that no ruler had believed, he put their own law to them about hearing a man before judging him, and at the burial he came with a hundred pound weight of myrrh and aloes and wound the body with Joseph (John 7:45-52; John 19:38-42).
offenseFull: There was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews, who came to Christ by night and said they knew he was a teacher come from God, because no man could do those miracles unless God were with him

(John 3:1-2). Those men taught the synagogues, and coming openly would have cost him his standing, so he came in the dark; he was a secret disciple. The answer he got was not a welcome but a requirement: except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God (John 3:3). He took it in the flesh and asked how a man can be born when he is old, and enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and was told that a man must be born of water and of the Spirit (John 3:4-5). Being born again is by the word of God, an incorruptible seed that lives and abides for ever (1 Peter 1:23); what is born of the flesh is flesh, and they that are in the flesh cannot please God (John 3:6-8; Romans 8:8). Esdras puts the same demand plainly: subdue your own understanding and reform your hearts (2 Esdras 14:34). That is a hard word to a man who already believes he is right, which is why sinners and publicans received Christ sooner than a ruler did.

He was asked whether he was a master of Israel and did not know these things (John 3:9-10). Men depended on him for the understanding of the law. Later, when the council sent officers to take Christ and raged that none of the rulers had believed on him, Nicodemus asked them whether their law judges a man before it hears him, and was answered with a sneer about Galilee (John 7:45-52). The law he invoked is written: hear the causes between brethren and judge righteously, and make diligent inquisition (Deuteronomy 1:16-17; Deuteronomy 19:18). At the burial he came bringing about a hundred pound weight of myrrh and aloes, and wound the body with Joseph in the linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury (John 19:38-42). His appearances move from a night visit, to a demand for a lawful hearing, to costly service in the daylight.
judgmentFull: The teaching he was given is the heart of that chapter. As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up (John 3:14-15). The history behind it is plain and so is who it was for: it was Israel in the wilderness that spoke against God and against Moses, Israel that was bitten, and Israel that looked and lived (Numbers 21:5-9). The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, given to put them in remembrance of the commandment of the law (Wisdom of Solomon 16:5-6), so the looking was never apart from repentance. The verse that follows, that God so loved the world (John 3:16), comes straight off the serpent and has the same people in view: the world John names elsewhere is the one Christ was made manifest to (John 1:29-31), the one the Pharisees said was gone after him (John 12:19), and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple (John 18:20).

Then the condemnation: light is come into the world and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil, while the man who does truth comes to the light so that his deeds may be made manifest (John 3:19-21). A man can be comfortable and even do well in the darkness he was raised in, and coming into the light costs him change. Christ did not condemn the rulers; they condemned themselves by not humbling down to repent. Nicodemus is the one of them who did come to the light, and the record of it is his deeds, not a sentence pronounced over him. The man first identified as coming by night is named again at the tomb (John 19:39). What he lacked at the first meeting he was still being called out of, and in the end he answered, at his own risk and his own cost.

text.text: There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews:
The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him.
Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?
Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.
That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.
The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.
Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.
Nicodemus answered and said unto him, How can these things be?
Jesus answered and said unto him, Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things?
Then came the officers to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why have ye not brought him?
The officers answered, Never man spake like this man.
Then answered them the Pharisees, Are ye also deceived?
Have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him?
But this people who knoweth not the law are cursed.
Nicodemus saith unto them, (he that came to Jesus by night, being one of them,)
Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?
They answered and said unto him, Art thou also of Galilee? Search, and look: for out of Galilee ariseth no prophet.
And I charged your judges at that time, saying, Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.

Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s: and the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.
And the judges shall make diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness be a false witness, and hath testified falsely against his brother;

And after this Joseph of Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus.
And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight.
Then took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury.
Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new sepulchre, wherein was never man yet laid.
There laid they Jesus therefore because of the Jews’ preparation day; for the sepulchre was nigh at hand.
And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:
That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.
And the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.

Therefore the people came to Moses, and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord, and against thee; pray unto the Lord, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.
And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
For when the horrible fierceness of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, thy wrath endured not for ever:
But they were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law.
The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.
This is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man which is preferred before me: for he was before me.
And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water.
The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.
Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing.
And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.
But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.
And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight.
